children.name: Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows
children.blurb: Agentic drafting and multi-model workflows describe a way of producing literary and narrative material where software systems take on planning, drafting, and revision tasks with limited human prompting, and where different generative models are used together for text, image, audio, or video.

sections.body: This field covers the use of artificial intelligence in writing fiction and narrative content. Current work includes systems that draft prose from prompts, generate outlines, propose dialogue, track story continuity, and offer developmental feedback. These tools are used by writers to produce rough material, explore alternatives, and check for inconsistencies. The focus is on practical assistance with the mechanics of storytelling rather than autonomous authorship. AI is being applied to tasks like expanding a scene, suggesting a character's reply, or flagging where a plot thread was dropped.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Drafting and dialogue generation are functional for short passages but often produce generic or repetitive prose over longer stretches. Outlining and continuity tracking are more reliable because they operate on structured data, yet they still miss subtle thematic connections and can misread a writer's intent. Developmental editing remains the least solved area, as current systems can identify surface problems like pacing or repeated words but struggle with deeper questions of motivation, tone, and emotional payoff. Honest limits include a lack of long-term memory across a full novel, difficulty maintaining a consistent voice without heavy human correction, and no reliable way to judge whether a suggested change improves the story.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section move from generation to revision. Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows explains how writers chain different models to produce and refine text, and a reader would go there to understand the basic mechanics of getting words on the page. Outlining and Plot Structure covers the planning stage, showing how AI can help arrange beats and arcs before drafting begins. Character Voice and Dialogue focuses on the narrower problem of making each speaker sound distinct, while World-Building and Continuity addresses the tracking of settings, rules, and facts across a manuscript. Developmental Editing sits at the end because it deals with the hardest part, evaluating and improving a complete draft rather than producing new material.
